why: The gate suite grew by accretion until releasing became impractical: every RCA added a gate and nothing ever measured what the set cost. Static context had the identical failure mode and was fixed by declaring a ceiling and making it a hard failure (B-110). This applies that pattern to time. A stage over its ceiling is a FAILURE, not a warning -- raising a ceiling is a deliberate, recorded decision, exactly as it is for context.
honest-limit: Seconds are host-dependent. Ceilings sit at roughly 2x the maintainer-box observation ON PURPOSE: this gate exists to catch a stage growing several-fold, NOT to police a 20% swing between a loaded and an idle box. If CI ever enforces these it needs its own ceilings measured from its own runners -- do not reuse these numbers there.
baseline-host: maintainer Windows box, 12 cores, 2026-08-07, measured idle

ceiling-revisions.why: B-217 added a required migration matrix for retiring the GitHub skill mirror safely. Two comparable v0.82.0 release attempts passed every functional gate but the hard budget correctly refused the meta-suite at 802.6s and 828.4s against 650s; their total local-gate times remained 910.5s and 938.2s. InstallerConvergence grew from 12 to 18 assertions and the new cases require 14 cross-shell installer executions covering first/repeat install, missing/malformed manifest, modified content, unknown content, and uninspectable-state preservation. Removing or collapsing those cases would discard the release-specific safety evidence. Set to about 1.45x the worse observation (828.4s), consistent with the recorded loaded-host policy and still able to catch a material regression. No functional test or behavior check was removed; the only enforcement relaxation is this recorded stage ceiling and its mechanically derived aggregate, reflecting the observed cost of the enlarged contract.

Recomputed exactly after the justified meta-suite revision: compose 60 + dist-gates 700 + meta-suite 1200 + eval-selftest 120 = 2080. This preserves B-139's same-commit consistency requirement; it is bookkeeping, not an independent allowance for slower gates. The worse observed total was 938.2s.

Not a load or growth adjustment -- a correction of a bookkeeping gap. The 2026-08-08 meta-suite revision below correctly raised that stage's own ceiling 300 -> 650 for a genuine, justified reason (B-67), but never recomputed total-local-gates to match. With dist-gates already at 700 (set 2026-08-07) and meta-suite at 650, their sum alone (1350) already exceeded the 1000 aggregate before compose/eval-selftest are even added -- meaning both stages could never legitimately run near their own already-justified ceilings and still pass the aggregate. Two consecutive v0.52.1 release attempts hit exactly this: every individual stage passed its own ceiling comfortably (dist-gates 668.4s/609.4s < 700; meta-suite 554.4s/527.3s < 650) while the aggregate still failed. Set to the literal sum of the current per-stage ceilings (60+700+650+120=1530), the minimum value under which a release cannot be blocked by this file's own internal inconsistency alone. This is NOT a response to a genuine slowdown -- ValidateDist.Tests.ps1, the single largest cost (339.6s of a 504.4s serial meta-suite reading, measured in isolation), has not changed since before the 2026-08-08 revision; see B-138 (the real fix -- per-assertion process-spawn cost is the actual scaling problem and belongs there, not in this ceiling) and B-139 (a same-commit gate so a per-stage ceiling change can never again drift out of sync with the aggregate silently).

B-67 (validate-dist checks 7) added a new markdown-link scan over every line of every shipped doc, plus ~7 new ValidateDist.Tests.ps1 cases exercising it across multiple scratch-dist copies -- genuine new scope, not noise. Two consecutive v0.51.3 release attempts refused on this gate, and got WORSE not better (341.6s, then 424.2s), which is what a real baseline shift under load looks like rather than a one-off contention spike. Not measured on an idle box -- this session had many worktrees and background processes running for hours, so these numbers are pessimistic vs. the honest-limit's idle-box assumption. Followed the same policy as the dist-gates revision: ~1.5x the worse observation (424.2 * 1.5 = 636.3), rounded to 650s. This still catches a doubling from here; it does not certify that 650s is the true idle baseline, which is unmeasured and should be re-taken on a quiet box and revised again if it lands meaningfully under this ceiling.

The 420 was a GUESS. I declared a ceiling for the one stage I had never actually timed -- I had measured the meta suite, ValidateDist.Tests and the section-path check, but never the dist gates as a stage. The first real release run measured 459.4s and the gate refused the release, which is the mechanism working correctly on its first outing and catching its author. Raised to 700s: ~1.5x the observation, which still catches a doubling but tolerates a loaded box. Recorded rather than quietly edited, because a ceiling that moves without a reason is not a ceiling.
Observed 12.0s. A 240s ceiling on a 12s stage would let it grow 20x before complaining, which is not a budget. Tightened.

observed-seconds._comment: Before/after for the 2026-08-07 gate-runtime work. Recorded so the improvement is checkable rather than asserted, and so the next regression has a number to be measured against.
observed-seconds._release-run-2026-08-07: First full release run with the budget live: compose 4.9, dist-gates 459.4, meta-suite 164.5, eval-selftest 12.0, total 640.8.

next-target: The pre-v0.74 local dist-gates shape ran three per-dist suites in parallel, each spawning ~234 fresh pwsh/bash processes (122 ps1 + 112 sh, measured on dotnet). Process creation, not CPU, is the bound. A 2026-08-22 audit found all 20 current dist hook test files byte-identical across dotnet, angular, and monorepo (not the stale historical '4 of 12' statement), but that does not make their executions equivalent. B-170 tried one sequential monorepo suite: it was functionally green (20 files, 0 failures) but took 924.1s and made dist-gates 1004.0s, so local release now runs zero shipped dist hook suites. It retains validate-dist x3 plus the full default-throttled root meta suite; CI still requires all three dists on both hosts before tag. No final speedup or budget change is recorded here.
the-trap-worth-remembering: The first cut of the parallel meta runner launched all ten files at once and came in at 1,335s against a 399s serial baseline -- 3.3x SLOWER, not faster. These suites are bound by process creation, not CPU, and ValidateDist.Tests parallelises its own cases, so unthrottled outer concurrency multiplied into hundreds of competing children. Throttling the outer loop and handing each file an inner lane budget is what turned it into a 2.7x win. Measure a parallelism change; do not assume it.
